stats.fact: ASSERT is developed by Microsoft Responsible AI organization and released as open-source under MIT license
ASSERT stands for Adaptive Spec-driven Scoring for Evaluation and Regression Testing
Initial release v0.1.0 on June 2, 2026; 27 forks, 24 open issues as of July 2026
Supports 100+ model endpoints via LiteLLM integration (Bedrock, Azure, OpenAI, VertexAI, Cohere, Anthropic, Sagemaker, HuggingFace, VLLM, NVIDIA NIM)
Supports 33+ agent frameworks via OpenInference auto-instrumentation (LangGraph, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, DSPy, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, etc.)
Core method is AI-assisted systematization following Agarwal et al. (2026) from Microsoft Research
Pipeline has 4 stages: Systematize → Test Set Generation → Inference → Judge
All artifacts are local-first JSON/JSONL files under artifacts/results/ — no hosted control plane required
Includes ACS (Agent Control Specification) adapter to turn evaluation findings into deployable runtime guardrails
Includes local web viewer (Node.js app) for browsing evaluation artifacts, taxonomy, and run comparisons
Bloom (predecessor) has 1,365 stars; Petri has 1,261 stars — ASSERT builds on their design philosophy

angles: ASSERT closes the gap between natural-language specifications and executable evaluations — most AI evaluation starts with generic benchmarks, not the actual product requirements
Trace-grounded judgment is a key differentiator: the judge can cite tool calls, routing decisions, and intermediate model calls as evidence, not just the final response
Framework-agnostic design means it works with any agent framework (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI SDK, etc.) through the callable target + OTel instrumentation
The ACS adapter creates a closed loop: evaluate → find violations → generate guardrails → deploy → re-evaluate
Microsoft's entry into the open-source AI evaluation space signals enterprise-grade investment in responsible AI tooling
Local-first architecture (no hosted control plane) makes it suitable for CI/CD pipelines and air-gapped environments
